introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section 1 is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section 2 in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section 2 answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark(s) for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A polythene rod rubbed with dry cloth becomes charged.

(i) State the type of charge the rod acquires. *[1 mark]*

(ii) Explain the origin of the charge on the rod. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The polythene rod acquires a **negative** charge.

(ii) Rubbing transfers **electrons** (negative charges) by friction: electrons move from the cloth to the polythene. The rod therefore has **an excess of electrons** and is negatively charged, while the cloth, which has lost electrons, becomes positively charged. Only electrons move; the protons stay in the nuclei, and the total charge is conserved (the charge gained by the rod equals the charge lost by the cloth).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 2 shows an electric circuit.

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2026-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_3_fig_1.png)

*Figure 2*

Calculate:

(i) the total resistance of the circuit. *[3 marks]*

(ii) the current flowing through the ammeter. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The $3\,\Omega$ and $6\,\Omega$ resistors are in **parallel**:

$\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{2}{6} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so $R_p = 2\,\Omega$.

This combination is in **series** with the $4\,\Omega$ resistor:

$$R_{\text{total}} = R_p + 4 = 2 + 4 = 6\,\Omega$$

The total resistance of the circuit is **$6\,\Omega$** (the ammeter and the cell are taken to have negligible resistance).

(ii) The ammeter is in series with the cell, so it reads the total current:

$$I = \dfrac{V}{R_{\text{total}}} = \dfrac{24\,\mathrm{V}}{6\,\Omega} = 4\,\mathrm{A}$$

The current through the ammeter is **$4\,\mathrm{A}$**.
